title: Section 223 — Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant

content.overview: Section 223 — Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. The operative rule is the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Cite the BNS section, not the repealed Indian Penal Code, for conduct governed by the BNS. Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. Historical concordance: IPC 189. For conduct governed by the BNS, cite BNS section 223; the IPC reference is historical concordance. Punishment, ingredients and exceptions are only those the section states. Not a verified closure.

sections.body: An order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, directing that a religious procession shall not pass down a certain street. A knowingly disobeys the order, and thereby causes danger of riot. A has committed the offence defined in this section

sections.heading: Explanations
sections.body: Explanation.—It is not necessary that the offender should intend to produce harm, or contemplate his disobedience as likely to produce harm. It is sufficient that he knows of the order which he disobeys, and that his disobedience produces, or is likely to produce, harm

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 223 (Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 223 (Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant), Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, knowing that, by an order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, he is directed to abstain from a certain act, or to take certain order with certain property in his possession or under his management, disobeys such direction,–
   (2) (a) shall, if such disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk of obstruction, annoyance or injury, to any person lawfully employed, be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both;
   (3) (b) and where such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 223 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 223 deals with Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. It sits in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. BNS restatement of IPC 189. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 189. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 223 is the rule on “Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant”. The section provides that whoever, knowing that, by an order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, he is directed to abstain from a certain act, or to take certain order with certain property in his possession or under his management, disobeys such direction,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. Whoever, knowing that, by an order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, he is directed to abstain from a certain act, or to take certain order with certain property in his possession or under his management, disobeys such direction,–
2. (a) shall, if such disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk of obstruction, annoyance or injury, to any person lawfully employed, be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both;
3. (b) and where such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both

Illustrations. The section itself supplies worked examples. In legal analysis, pick one illustration, restate its facts, and show which ingredient it proves. Illustration (a): An order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, directing that a religious procession shall not pass down a certain street. A knowingly disobeys the order, and thereby causes danger of riot. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Explanations. Explanation.—It is not necessary that the offender should intend to produce harm, or contemplate his disobedience as likely to produce harm. It is sufficient that he knows of the order which he disobeys, and that his disobedience produces, or is likely to produce, harm An explanation is not optional commentary. It is part of the section and must appear in an authoritative brief.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 223. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Conclusion. BNS s. 223 is the complete current-law heading for Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 223 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIII (Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant under Section 223 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 223.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 223 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 223 vs General Attempt: Section 223 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 223 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 223 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 223 for conduct relating to disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant.
Rule: Under BNS s. 223, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 223.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 223 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
